{"obligations": {"reduction": {"status": "not_written", "quote": "When the players alternately select pieces of a fixed multiset \(L\), Liu Bang first, Liu Bang’s optimal total equals
\[
V(L)=\frac12\Bigl(\sum L+D(L)\Bigr).
\]
(The optimum is realised by always selecting a currently longest remaining piece.)", "witness": "What must be proved for all cases: that in the alternating claiming game on an arbitrary finite multiset L, greedy (take a currently longest piece) is optimal for both players, so that the first player's optimal total is exactly (sum L + D(L))/2, where D is the alternating sum of the sorted lengths. The quoted passage merely asserts this value and asserts greedy optimality in a parenthetical; no exchange/strategy-stealing argument, no induction on |L|, and no proof that the opponent cannot do better than greedy appears anywhere in the text.", "load_bearing": "Every later step works with D(M) instead of the actual game value, so the whole equivalence between 'Liu gets at least 2^n/S' and 'D(M) >= 1' rests on this unproved identity."}, "lower_bound": {"status": "written_but_invalid", "quote": "Observe that the mass \(2^n-\mu\) together with all pieces of \(P\) may be viewed as a subdivision of a stick of length \(2^n-\mu+\sum P=S_n-\mu\le S_{n-1}\) performed with at most \(m+(k-1)\le n-1\) cuts.", "witness": "COUNTEREXAMPLE to the asserted inequality S_n - mu <= S_{n-1}, which only requires mu > tau = 2^{n-1}. Take n = 2, so B_2 = {1,2,4}, S_2 = 7, S_1 = 3, tau = 2. Use t = 1 <= n cut, placed inside the bin of length 4 at distance 3.5, so k = 1, m = 0, P = {1,2}, Q = {3.5,0.5}, mu = 3.5 > tau = 2 (subcase hypothesis holds). Then S_n - mu = 7 - 3.5 = 3.5 > 3 = S_1, contradicting the claimed bound. Consequently the dummy piece of length S_{n-1} - (S_n - mu) = -0.5 has negative length and the ensuing appeal to the inductive hypothesis on a padded copy of B_{n-1} is vacuous. (The text also silently identifies this dummy length with d = mu - tau, whereas S_{n-1}-(S_n-mu) = mu - 2^n, a different quantity.)", "load_bearing": "The whole k>=1, mu>tau subcase derives D(M)>=1 from applying the induction hypothesis to the padded remainder; with the padding step invalid the subcase has no proof, and the remaining text there ('something that forces', 'the worst case', numerical checks for n<=3) supplies no substitute."}, "upper_bound": {"status": "not_written", "quote": "XY aims to realise a refinement whose pieces can be perfectly matched into pairs of equal length except for a single leftover piece of length \(1\). Such a multiset has \(D=1\).", "witness": "What must be proved for all cases: for EVERY multiset L of total S = 2^{n+1}-1 arising from Liu's at most n marks, an explicit choice of at most n additional cuts yielding D(M) <= 1 (e.g. a subset-sum/pigeonhole gap bound plus a pairing construction). The quoted passage only states a target shape (paired pieces plus one leftover of length 1) and the following text admits the counting fails ('is exactly the number of internal breaks, which is 2n; but starting from an already partially cut stick the residual number of cuts required is at most n'), with no proof that n cuts suffice from an arbitrary Liu partition; the section elsewhere records its own contradiction ('This appears contradictory unless...') and closes with checks for n = 1, 2 only.", "load_bearing": "Tightness of c_n = 2^n/(2^{n+1}-1) rests entirely on Theorem C; without a construction valid for every Liu partition and every n the upper bound is unestablished."}}, "S_valid": 0, "wrong_answer_stated": false, "notes": "Correct closed form stated. Reduction to the alternating sum is asserted, not proved. Lower-bound induction breaks at a false padding inequality (S_n-mu <= S_{n-1}) and defers to n<=3 numerics. Upper bound is a garbled sketch with self-admitted contradictions and only n=1,2 checks."}
